identification.summary: Gray Sandstorm (formerly DEV-0343) is an Iran-origin actor that Microsoft says runs extensive password spraying against Office 365 / Exchange accounts. It emulates a Firefox browser and routes traffic through Tor proxy IPs [S1][S3]. In 2021 Microsoft observed it spraying more than 250 Office 365 tenants, compromising fewer than 20. Targets were US and Israeli defense technology firms, geographic information systems (GIS) companies, Persian Gulf ports of entry and maritime/cargo shippers with a Middle East presence [S1]. In March 2026 Check Point Research reported an Iran-nexus Microsoft 365 password-spray campaign against Israeli and UAE municipalities and companies, with tradecraft similar to Gray Sandstorm [S4][S5][S6].
identification.firstObserved: Microsoft began tracking the DEV-0343 cluster in late July 2021 [S1]. The imported summary's claim of activity 'since at least 2012' is not supported by any source gathered here.
identification.notes: Microsoft name: Gray Sandstorm. Gray Sandstorm was formerly tracked as DEV-0343 [S3]; 'DEV-' names are temporary designations Microsoft gives to unknown, emerging or developing clusters of activity [S1]. No MITRE ATT&CK group entry was identified. Microsoft documented an overlap with EUROPIUM (now Hazel Sandstorm): in June 2021 DEV-0343 targeted the same account within minutes of EUROPIUM gaining access, which Microsoft assesses as coordination among Iranian actors [S2]. Check Point also tied the 2026 technique to Peach Sandstorm, a separate Microsoft cluster [S4][S6]. Keep these clusters distinct.

attribution.sponsor: Iran. Microsoft lists Gray Sandstorm's origin as Iran [S3] and assesses its activity 'likely' supports the national interests of the Islamic Republic of Iran [S1][S2]. No source gathered names a specific government organization (e.g., IRGC or MOIS).
attribution.confidence: Microsoft's wording is 'likely' supports Iranian national interests [S1]. For the 2026 campaign, coverage reports that Check Point assessed Iranian responsibility with moderate confidence, citing similarities to Gray Sandstorm [S4][S6]. Hive Pro attributed the activity with moderate confidence to an Iran-nexus actor whose tactics closely mirror Gray Sandstorm, which is not a confirmed identification [S7]. No government attribution was found.
attribution.basis: Microsoft cited pattern-of-life analysis, notably activity Sunday through Thursday during Iranian working hours. It also cited extensive geographic and sectoral overlap with known Iranian actors and alignment of techniques and targets with another Iran-origin actor [S1][S2]. Check Point's 2026 assessment rests on Microsoft 365 log analysis showing red-team tooling run through Tor exit nodes, similar to Gray Sandstorm, plus target correlation with Iranian missile strikes [S4][S6].

objectives: Microsoft assesses that DEV-0343 sought to track adversary security services and Middle East maritime shipping to strengthen Iran's contingency plans. It also suggests that commercial satellite imagery and proprietary shipping plans or logs could help offset Iran's developing satellite program [S1]. Check Point judged that the March 2026 campaign against municipalities likely supported kinetic operations and bomb damage assessment (BDA), as reported in coverage [S4][S6].

sectors: Defense technology: military-grade radars, drone technology, satellite systems, emergency response communications [S1][S2]
Geographic information systems (GIS) and spatial analytics [S1][S2]
Ports of entry and maritime/cargo transportation [S1][S2]
Municipalities and government entities (2026, Check Point, similar tradecraft) [S4][S5][S6]
Technology, transportation and logistics, healthcare, manufacturing (2026, Check Point) [S4][S6]
regions: Limited 2026 targeting in Europe, US, UK and Saudi Arabia [S4][S5]
targeting.notes: The 2021 targeting comes from Microsoft [S1][S2]. Reporting on the 2026 campaign comes from Check Point via secondary coverage, with attribution resting on tradecraft similarity [S4][S5][S6][S7]. Coverage reported more than 300 organizations targeted in Israel and more than 25 in the UAE [S5].

capabilities.summary: The actor's core capability is low-cost credential access. It uses an enumeration and password-spray tool similar to the open-source o365spray against Exchange ActiveSync and Autodiscover endpoints to validate accounts and passwords [S1][S2]. It sprays dozens to hundreds of accounts per organization, enumerating each one dozens to thousands of times. Traffic comes from 150 to more than 1,000 unique Tor exit IPs per organization, with Firefox or Chrome user agents [S1]. Because the Tor infrastructure rotates, Microsoft published no static IOCs [S1]. Microsoft notes that accounts with MFA are resilient to these sprays [S1][S8]. In the 2026 campaign Check Point reported several behaviors. Scanning ran from frequently rotated Tor exit nodes with an Internet Explorer 10 user agent. Operators then logged in with valid credentials via Windscribe and NordVPN IPs geolocated in Israel to bypass geographic restrictions [S4][S6]. No custom malware or exploited CVEs are attributed in the sources gathered.

campaigns.name: Account targeting alongside EUROPIUM
campaigns.summary: DEV-0343 targeted an account within minutes of EUROPIUM (Hazel Sandstorm) gaining access to it on 13 June 2021. Microsoft cited this as coordination among Iranian actors.

campaigns.name: Office 365 password-spray campaign against defense, GIS and maritime
campaigns.summary: Starting in late July 2021, DEV-0343 sprayed more than 250 Office 365 tenants through Tor, compromising fewer than 20. Targets were US/Israeli defense technology firms, GIS companies, Persian Gulf ports and maritime shippers. Microsoft disclosed the campaign on 11 October 2021.

campaigns.name: MSTIC CyberWarCon 2021 briefing
campaigns.summary: Microsoft placed DEV-0343 within broader Iranian trends and reiterated its targets, o365spray-like tooling and Iran working-hours pattern.

campaigns.name: Iran-nexus Microsoft 365 password spray against Israel and UAE (similar tradecraft)
campaigns.summary: Check Point reported three spray waves on 3, 13 and 23 March 2026, mainly against municipalities in Israel and the UAE. It assessed the campaign as Iran-linked with similarities to Gray Sandstorm, and correlated targets with cities hit by Iranian missiles (possible BDA support).

diamond.adversary: Iran-origin operators working Sunday through Thursday during Iranian business hours. Microsoft assesses they likely serve Iranian national interests [S1][S2][S3].
diamond.capability: An o365spray-like enumeration and password-spray tool against Exchange ActiveSync/Autodiscover; per Check Point in 2026, red-team tooling followed by valid-account logins [S1][S2][S4].
diamond.infrastructure: Rotating Tor exit nodes, 150 to 1,000+ per target organization [S1]. In 2026, commercial VPN egress (Windscribe, NordVPN) geolocated in Israel [S4][S6].
diamond.victim: Office 365 tenants of defense technology, GIS, port and maritime organizations in the US, Israel and the Gulf [S1]. In 2026, Israeli and UAE municipalities and companies [S4][S5].
diamond.socioPolitical: Iranian contingency planning against adversary security services and Gulf shipping, plus satellite-program support [S1]. In 2026, possible support to kinetic targeting and BDA during Iran-Israel hostilities [S4][S6].
diamond.technology: Cloud identity: Office 365 / Microsoft 365 authentication via legacy ActiveSync and Autodiscover endpoints, and accounts without MFA or Conditional Access [S1][S4].

gaps: Check Point's primary report could not be fetched (host unreachable from this environment). Its 2026 details, including the 'moderate confidence' wording, IE10 user agent, VPN providers and BDA judgment, come from search-result summaries and secondary coverage.
The 2026 campaign is attributed to Gray Sandstorm only by tradecraft similarity. Check Point also cites Peach Sandstorm, and Microsoft has not publicly confirmed Gray Sandstorm's involvement.
The imported summary claims activity since at least 2012; no cited source supports this, and Microsoft dates the DEV-0343 cluster to July 2021.
Sponsoring organization (IRGC, MOIS or a contractor) is not identified in any source gathered.
Post-compromise actions after the 2021 compromise of fewer than 20 tenants (data accessed, persistence, follow-on tooling) are not public.
No MITRE ATT&CK group entry was found; no independent vendor or government reporting on Gray Sandstorm between 2022 and 2025 was found.
The relationship to Hazel Sandstorm (EUROPIUM) beyond the single June 2021 coordinated-access event is unclear.
The Microsoft threat actor naming page in the imported references was not re-fetched.
The date of Microsoft's conversion of DEV-0343 to the Gray Sandstorm name (often given as April 2023) was not confirmed by any cited source; the claim was removed.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1 (operational environment): Key cyber terrain is cloud identity, meaning Microsoft 365 / Exchange Online tenants of defense contractors (radar, UAS, satellite, emergency communications), GIS providers, Gulf ports and maritime logistics, and, per 2026 reporting, host-nation municipalities [S1][S4]. STEP 2 (effects): Iran's working-week pattern (Sunday through Thursday, about 04:00 to 16:00 UTC) and Tor-based spraying mean noisy but persistent authentication attempts against legacy protocols. Accounts with MFA are resilient [S1][S2]. STEP 3 (adversary model): enumeration via ActiveSync/Autodiscover, then password spray from Tor, then a valid-account login (in 2026 via in-country VPN egress), then mailbox access [S1][S4][S6]. STEP 4 (COAs): MLCOA is continued spraying of defense-industrial, logistics and maritime tenants to collect imagery, shipping and security-service information for Iranian contingency planning [S1]. MDCOA, during Iran-related hostilities, is compromise of host-nation municipal or logistics accounts near US or partner installations to support Iranian targeting and BDA, as Check Point suggested for March 2026 [S4][S6]. Candidate indicators: high-volume failed sign-ins to ActiveSync/Autodiscover from Tor exit IPs; Firefox, Chrome or IE10 user agents on legacy endpoints; successful logins from commercial VPN ranges geolocated in-country soon after spray activity; and spray timing aligned to Iranian business hours [S1][S4][S6].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: fuse Entra ID / M365 sign-in telemetry (failed-logon sequences, Tor exit matches, legacy-protocol use) into the common operational picture. Microsoft published no static IOCs, so detection must be behavioral [S1]. (2) Authorities: most targets are defense contractors, logistics firms and foreign municipalities outside the DODIN, so response depends on DIB partnerships, host-nation coordination and vendor reporting rather than direct DoD action [S1][S4]. (3) Mission assurance: enforce MFA, block legacy ActiveSync clients from bypassing Conditional Access, and block anonymizer traffic. These are Microsoft's recommended mitigations, and they directly negate this TTP [S1]. Logistics, port and contractor accounts that support theater sustainment are priority assets. (4) Coordination: during Iran-related crises, share spray indicators with host-nation and coalition CERTs (Israel, UAE, Gulf partners), since municipal compromise may precede or support kinetic strikes [S4][S5].
